newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-UK global trade deficit to narrow in July.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-UK global trade deficit to narrow in July.

text.p: British data due on Thursday will show the country's global trade deficit narrowed in July but is also likely to reveal the trade balance with non-EU countries moved further into the red in August, economists said.
A Reuter poll of economists found a consensus forecasting a global deficit of 775 million stg in July, down from June's 1.12 billion gap.
August's deficit with non-EU countries will expand to 750 million stg from 506 million in July. But July's deficit was the lowest since May 1995, analysts said.
"It seems reasonable to expect the non-EU deficit to rebound somewhat from July's very low level," said Jonathan Loynes, UK economist at HSBC Markets.
Ciaran Barr, UK economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said the low non-EU deficit in July, suggested Britain's global trade deficit for that month must fall.
But the overall figure, although set to drop, would conceal a reversal of the falling deficit with EU countries, he said.
"EU import growth seems too low given the evident pick-up in domestic consumer demand and we expect this to rise in coming months, placing upward pressure on the whole world deficit," he said.
